steps.name: QC and DESeq2 differential expression, cases vs controls
caveats: Single batch, no additional covariates in metadata — cannot adjust for confounders that are not recorded; note this limitation in the summary rather than inventing a covariate
12000 gene rows is a pre-filtered/annotated matrix (not full ~20k+ transcriptome), likely already gene-symbol collapsed — do not re-collapse or assume Ensembl IDs are present
Verify metadata has exactly the two expected condition labels and 60/60 split before fitting; report discrepancy rather than silently proceeding if it does not match
steps.context: Input: /eval-four-models-without-population-n60-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (raw Salmon gene-level integer counts, gene symbol column + 120 sample columns) and /eval-four-models-without-population-n60-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (120 samples x condition, case/control, single batch, unpaired). This is the foundational DE step all downstream effect-size and enrichment work depends on.
steps.question: Which of the 12000 genes are differentially expressed between the 60 cases and 60 controls in whole blood, using raw Salmon gene counts?
acceptance_criteria: Counts matrix (12000 genes x 120 samples) and metadata (120 samples x condition) are loaded and sample order/names are verified to match between the two files before building the DESeqDataSet
Low-count genes are filtered (e.g. require count >=10 in at least 60 samples, the smaller group size) before running DESeq2
DESeq2 is run with design ~ condition (single batch, no covariates available in metadata beyond condition) and a Wald test contrast of case vs control
Output table has one row per gene with baseMean, raw log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj
A separate shrunken log2FoldChange (apeglm if the coefficient parameterization allows it, else ashr as fallback) is computed and reported alongside the raw log2FoldChange
PCA plot and sample-sample correlation/dispersion diagnostic plots are produced to confirm no unexpected outliers or single-batch assumption violation
Full results table (raw counts, normalized counts, DE stats, shrunken LFC) is saved for downstream steps

steps.name: Effect-size triage: significance vs magnitude classification
caveats: A fixed |log2FC|>=1 threshold is a convention, not a biological law — state it as a chosen convention and consider reporting sensitivity at |log2FC|>=0.5 and >=1.5 as a robustness check

Genes with low baseMean can have inflated shrunken LFC estimates even after shrinkage; flag very low baseMean genes in the 'large-effect' tier rather than presenting them with the same confidence as high-count genes
steps.context: Consumes the DESeq2 results table (raw + shrunken log2FC, padj) from T1S1. Directly operationalizes the research question's distinction between 'differ' (statistical test) and 'differ enough to matter' (effect size).
steps.question: Among genes significantly different between cases and controls (padj < 0.05), which have a shrunken log2 fold-change large enough to be biologically meaningful (e.g. |log2FC| >= 1, i.e. >=2-fold), versus statistically significant but small-magnitude changes?
acceptance_criteria: Classifies every tested gene into a 2x2 grid: significant-and-large-effect, significant-but-small-effect, non-significant-but-large-effect (nominal effect only, flagged as underpowered/exploratory), non-significant-and-small-effect
Uses the DESeq2 shrunken log2FoldChange (not the raw/unshrunken estimate) for the magnitude axis to avoid winner's-curse inflation of small-count genes
States the exact thresholds used (padj cutoff and |log2FC| cutoff) explicitly and justifies the fold-change cutoff relative to typical whole-blood RNA-seq effect sizes

Produces a volcano plot (log2FC vs -log10 padj) with the four-way classification colored, and a ranked table of the 'significant-and-large-effect' tier with gene symbol, baseMean, shrunken log2FC, padj
Reports counts of genes in each of the four tiers and the fraction of significant genes that clear the effect-size bar, directly answering that significance and magnitude are not the same thing here

steps.name: Whole-blood immune cell composition deconvolution
caveats: Whole blood (not PBMC) — deconvolution methods calibrated on PBMC/tumor microenvironment references may misestimate granulocyte-rich whole-blood composition; state this limitation
This step is exploratory context for interpreting T1S2, not a primary endpoint — do not let a partial or failed deconvolution block reporting of the core DE/effect-size results
steps.context: Uses normalized counts from T1S1 (whole blood, 60 case vs 60 control). No LM22 or xCell reference signature file was found in the reference store during planning, so this step is scoped to immunedeconv methods with self-contained signatures; if immunedeconv resolves its own bundled marker sets internally (as several of its methods do, independent of the external reference store), it should proceed and report which methods succeeded.
steps.question: Do cases and controls differ in estimated immune cell type proportions, and does the case/control DE signal from T1S1 plausibly reflect shifts in blood cell composition rather than purely intracellular transcriptional change?
acceptance_criteria: Runs immune cell deconvolution on the normalized bulk counts using method(s) from the immunedeconv package that ship their own built-in signature (e.g. quanTIseq, MCP-counter, EPIC) — do not attempt CIBERSORT/LM22 or xCell if their required signature files are not resolvable in the reference store; explicitly report which methods ran and which were skipped for missing signatures
Produces per-sample estimated cell-type fractions or scores and compares case vs control per cell type (Wilcoxon or t-test with multiple-testing correction across cell types)

Cross-references any cell-type composition differences against the top significant-and-large-effect genes from T1S2 to flag genes whose case/control difference is consistent with known cell-type marker genes (e.g. neutrophil or lymphocyte markers) rather than a compositionally-independent signal
Reports explicitly if no bundled-signature deconvolution method could run, rather than fabricating cell fractions

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of large-effect genes
caveats: Gene symbol matching: confirm counts.csv gene symbols use current HGNC nomenclature compatible with the GMT files; report any large fraction of unmatched genes rather than silently dropping them

ImmuneSigDB (C7) and TF/miRNA target sets are available but are computational/observational predictions, not curated pathways — do not use them as the primary enrichment call, only as optional supplementary context if requested later
steps.context: Consumes the gene tiers and ranked shrunken-log2FC gene list from T1S2. Reference gene sets confirmed present: WikiPathways human GMT, MSigDB human Hallmark/GO(BP,CC,MF)/canonical-pathways GMTs, all HGNC-symbol keyed matching the counts.csv gene symbol identifiers.
steps.question: What biological pathways and processes are over-represented among the genes classified as significant AND large-effect (the tier judged to 'matter') versus among all significant genes regardless of effect size?
acceptance_criteria: Runs over-representation analysis (or fgsea rank-based enrichment on the full shrunken-log2FC-ranked gene list) separately for: (a) the significant-and-large-effect tier gene list from T1S2, and (b) the full significant gene list regardless of effect size, so the two results can be contrasted
Tests against human WikiPathways gene sets and MSigDB human Hallmark, GO Biological Process, and canonical pathway (KEGG MEDICUS/BioCarta/PID) gene sets confirmed present in the reference store

Reports adjusted p-values (BH) for pathway hits and explicitly compares which pathways appear only in the full-significant list vs only in the large-effect tier, addressing whether effect-size filtering changes the biological interpretation
Collapses or notes redundancy among nested GO terms rather than reporting raw counts of overlapping hierarchical hits as independent findings

plan.title: Whole-blood case vs control DE with effect-size triage
plan.analytical_narrative: The data are raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 121 samples incl. header) for a balanced, unpaired 60 vs 60 whole-blood cohort with condition as the only metadata column, single batch. The question explicitly separates statistical significance from effect-size magnitude, so the plan runs a standard DESeq2 negative-binomial DE workflow with shrunken log2FC (apeglm/ashr), then applies an explicit dual-threshold triage (adjusted p-value AND |shrunken log2FC|) to distinguish 'differs' from 'differs enough to matter'. Because whole blood is a heterogeneous mixture, immune cell composition differences between cases and controls could produce or mask apparent gene-level differences, so an immune deconvolution step is included to check whether the DE signal tracks cell-composition shifts rather than intracellular regulation — this uses only the count matrix and public signature-based methods available in the sandbox (no LM22/xCell reference file was found in the reference store, so the deconvolution step is scoped to methods that ship their own signatures, e.g. quanTIseq/MCP-counter via immunedeconv, and will report explicitly if a method's bundled signature cannot be resolved rather than fabricate cell fractions). A downstream enrichment step interprets the effect-size-qualified gene list against human pathway gene sets (WikiPathways and MSigDB Hallmark/GO/canonical, all confirmed present for Homo sapiens) to give biological context to the 'matters' tier specifically, not the full significant-but-small-effect list. All steps operate on the actual 12000x120 count matrix and 120-sample metadata table; no dataset facts are invented.
